standard.title: Verbs anchored in tense
standard.description: understand that verbs are anchored in time through tense
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how compound sentences connect ideas using coordinating conjunctions (AC9E2LA06). They have encountered verbs but have not yet examined how tense anchors verbs to time — including the distinction between regular and irregular past tense forms.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand that verbs are anchored in time through tense, including regular and irregular past tense forms.

nodes.label: Tense anchors verbs in time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify present and past tense verbs and explain how tense anchors the action in time.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two verbs — one present tense, one past tense — and explain what time period each is anchored in.
nodes.typical_width: Learn how time is represented through verb tense — present tense anchors events now, past tense anchors them earlier — and identify tense in a range of texts including narratives and recounts.
wider: Examine why recounts use past tense while instructions typically use present tense, connecting tense choice to text purpose
Explore future tense forms and discuss how they anchor events differently from present and past
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who haven't grasped that tense anchors verbs in time at N1 lack the conceptual framework for N2 — understanding why regular and irregular past forms exist requires knowing what past tense is doing.

response_modes.reason: The concept of tense as time-anchoring is best grasped through examples across different text types — recounts use past, instructions use present, narratives mix both. Seeing tense as a systematic choice (not a verb ending rule) requires contrast across contexts.

success_criteria: Student identifies the tense of a verb (present or past)
Student explains what time period the tense anchors the event in

nodes.label: Regular and irregular past tense
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can form regular past tense by adding '-ed' and identify irregular past tense verbs that change form differently.
nodes.minimum_width: Form the past tense of at least two regular verbs correctly, and identify at least two irregular past tense verbs (e.g. 'ran', 'caught').
nodes.typical_width: Learn that regular past tense is formed by adding '-ed' (walked, jumped) and that irregular verbs change form differently (ran, caught, came); apply this knowledge in reading and writing.
wider: Collect a class list of common irregular past tense verbs, grouping them by their pattern of change
Find regular and irregular past tense verbs in a narrative text and discuss how they create the time frame of the story

response_modes.reason: Irregular past tense forms must be memorised — there are no rules to apply. Students need repeated exposure and practice rather than more contexts, which makes this a consolidation point rather than a hinge.

success_criteria: Student correctly forms regular past tense using '-ed'
Student correctly produces at least three irregular past tense forms
